title: Living in his grandfather's large household
summary: Cobb lived with his grandfather, a boilermaker with ten children who ran the house by his own law and bought food in bulk; his father died of tuberculosis.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, Arnett, when your father died, was that when you went to live with your friend's grandfather.
Yes, because he and my mother wasn't together.

And my mother was a domestic worker but he did this for me because, like all fathers would do, or some, showing their interest, you know. But I don't think it was two or three months later that he passed, but he was sick during that time, my mother told me. In later years she told me how it happened. And he died of tuberculosis.
Your grandfather, he had a really large family.

He had ten kids, seven girls, three boys. And he was a man that believed in living under his roof, you live by my law. And that's the way it went down. And he would buy food -- he'd feed you, you couldn't pay him anything. I
don't care if you had a job. You don't pay him anything to stay there, and he'll feed you because he bought everything in gross lots for his family.
What did he do for a living?

For (unintelligible) Boiler Works here in Houston, Texas. And I guess that he had a good salary if he could buy crates of eggs, ten pounds packs of potatoes, and what have you. That's the way he bought it. He didn't buy no little small lots for ten children, you know.
